newsitem.title: USA: Ensco Intl optimistic on dayrates.
newsitem.headline: Ensco Intl optimistic on dayrates.

text.p: Ensco International Inc believes that dayrates for jackup rigs will continue to expand, company chief executive Carl Thorne told a teleconference.
"We still have got a lot of room with what we are doing," he said.
Ensco said that in the second quarter dayrates for 250 foot jackups in the Gulf of Mexico had averaged $40,000 and were now in excess of $50,000.
The company said that it planned capital expenditures of $190-$200 million through to the end of this year and would upgrade some six rigs between now and the middle of next year.

Ensco said that it had two rigs under contract in India at dayrates of $27,000 compared with an average of $75,000 for that type in the Asian region and that one of those would be out of contract late in the third quarter of this year and another in the first quarter.
The rigs would then go to a dockyard for 90 days.
Thorne said that although he envisoned longer lead times on upgrades in the industry as a whole due to dockyard and material delays, Ensco has already shipyard space reserved.
However, despite the increase in rig dayrates, Thorne said said he did not anticipate a rash of new builds, which could depress rates in the industry.
"We are not yet at replacement cost pricing," Thorne said.
He said that to build a 350 foot Gulf of Mexico jackup would cost some $85-$90 million, while a 300 foot North Sea rig would cost $120-$140 million, and specialist rigs a great deal more.
He did however say that Ensco has a number of projects under active consideration.
Asked by analysts whether the company would consider a stock buyback or stock dividend, Thorne said that both had been considered but would not provide the best shareholder value.

Following on the proposed merger between offshore drillers Reading & Bates Corp and Falcon Drilling Co Inc , Thorne said that he did not see industry consolidation in the jackup market. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
